decisions.executionNote: Approach the hammer and tape measure from their respective sides, gradually turning the open grippers downward; tabletop height remains uncertain.
Retry with much smaller increments to establish a continuous elbow-up approach from the reset posture.
Continue smooth overhead positioning for hammer and tape, completing most of the downward wrist rotation.
Refine alignment over the visible hammer handle and tape measure using the closer wrist views; lower cautiously with open jaws.
Back off the contact, restore fully open jaws, and correct lateral alignment before another shallow descent.
Align around the hammer handle and tape body, descend a small amount, then close both grippers for a visual lift test.
Lift both closed grippers vertically and verify from RGB that the hammer and tape measure are retained before transferring.
The hammer did not rise with the left gripper; retry at a lower handle grasp. Keep the visibly retained tape closed and raise it clear.
Settle the lower hammer grasp and lift to test retention. Carry the retained tape toward the toolbox while inspecting the molded slots.
Both tools appear retained. Transfer the hammer above the left molded channel and tape above the square recess, keeping the arms separated.
Correct the rejected tensor without changing the planned approach: lower the right transport height while approaching slowly, both grippers closed.
Lower the right wrist without further forward reach to restore extension margin. Bring the hammer nearer its left-side channel at a lower height.
Retreat the right wrist from the IK limit and tilt its approach forward while retaining the tape. Continue the slower left-channel alignment.
Use submillimeter initial retreat increments at the right-arm continuity boundary, then gradually increase once clear; retain both tools.
Align the hammer with its long left recess and the tape with the square recess, using a forward-tilted right approach to avoid the reach limit.
Release the tape over its square pocket and withdraw the right jaws. Lift the hammer slightly and correct its visibly skewed orientation before seating.
Withdraw the released tape gripper toward the pliers. Raise the retained hammer clear of the box and continue correcting its skew before lowering again.
The tape is now outside the box and will need recovery. Approach the pliers handles; cautiously reorient the raised hammer based on its current visible direction.
The hammer appears to have slipped onto the box diagonally; reopen and approach its handle. Lower slightly and close on the centered pliers handles.
Regrasp the hammer handle now extending toward the front rim. Lift the closed pliers gripper vertically to confirm retention.
Lift the hammer grasp clear of the molding to let the jaws settle. Transfer the visibly retained pliers above the right-side channel without releasing.
Rotate the lifted hammer toward the slot's longitudinal direction. Shift the pliers inward over the right channel and lower slowly, keeping both grips closed.
The hammer stayed on the rim during the prior lift, so realign an open grasp directly over its diagonal handle. Seat and release the pliers in the right recess.
Close around the now-centered hammer handle and perform a small vertical retention test. Withdraw the open right gripper vertically from the placed pliers.
Clear the right arm away from the toolbox to avoid gripper interference. The hammer did not follow the last lift; prepare a deeper isolated left-arm grasp.
With the right arm clear, lower the open left jaws around the hammer handle to actual grasp depth, watching for contact rather than assuming retention.
Close the deeper isolated hammer grasp and test a short lift. Begin an angled right-arm approach to recover the tape beyond the box.
Lift the hammer without rotation to establish whether the new grasp holds. Advance and lower the tilted right jaws toward the displaced tape.
Move the hammer grasp to its protruding free handle, away from the obstructing rim. Refine the tape approach inward and down using the head-camera geometry.
Descend around the hammer's free handle and close. Close the right jaws at the geometrically aligned tape position, then pause before testing either grasp.
Test the free-end hammer grasp with a vertical lift. Correct the tape grasp to the right based on its clear offset from the closed jaws, then reclose.
Slowly raise and turn the hammer's free-end grasp toward its longitudinal slot. Lift the closed right gripper to check whether it retained the tape or only missed its body.
Raise and back the hammer away from the molding to clear its caught head. Reopen and move the right grasp farther onto the tape body rather than its near clip.
Bring the hammer's held handle end over the left channel while lowering and making a small yaw correction. Center the tape body from wrist-image motion and close again.
Back off the left tracking obstruction and tip the hanging hammer toward a horizontal placement. Lift and retreat with the newly centered tape grasp to verify retention.
Retry with a small continuity-preserving initial adjustment, then gently raise and tilt the hammer; lift the tape away from the tabletop.
Bridge the small remaining continuity mismatch before backing away from the hammer contact; keep the tape closed during its lift test.
Clear the left arm toward the remaining wrench and inspect the settled box. Retry the tape with a more nearly vertical, lower grasp rather than the slipping angled approach.
Approach the wrench handle with a restored vertical left gripper. Continue rightward and forward tape alignment based on the visible wrist offset, leaving both jaws open.
Move the wrench handle into the left grasp region. Extend the tape approach mainly by a small wrist tilt, avoiding further large right-arm reach.
Finish centering the wrench handle, then close both grippers and pause at the current tape-body alignment before lifting.
Perform straight vertical lifts with both grippers closed to verify retention of the wrench and tape before any transfer.
Both tools now visibly rise with their grippers. Retreat the right arm gently from its extension boundary and begin a separated transfer toward the toolbox.
Carry the tape slowly toward the square pocket and the wrench toward the left channels, correcting its small yaw while keeping the arms separated.
Lift the retained tape above the box rim before translating farther inward. Reopen and approach the wrench that slipped beside the box, matching its new diagonal orientation.
Grasp the wrench farther along its handle for better retention. Recover the dropped tape with the jaws rotated away from the adjacent toolbox wall.
Test the more central wrench grasp by lifting straight up. Offset the rotated right jaws over the tape body, descend slightly, and close.
Correct the rejected tensor without changing the plan: align the wrench over the left channels and withdraw the right jaws from the rim contact.
The wrench remained outside the box; approach its current handle again. Align the right gripper vertically over the relocated tape with the jaws clear of the rim.
Recenter using the observed tool-to-jaw offsets: leftward and forward over the wrench, slightly inward and forward over the tape. Turn the right jaws parallel to the box wall.
Lift the open left jaws out of the persistent hammer/rim obstruction before repositioning. Use a small right-wrist tilt, not more arm extension, to center the tape.
Restore the left grasp to vertical and descend over the wrench handle. Close on the centered tape body and test only a short vertical lift.
Close the centered wrench grasp and make a short lift. The tape is visibly retained; lift it clear of the rim while retreating enough to preserve right-arm reach margin.
Raise the wrench slightly above the obstructions, then transfer without changing its grasp orientation. The tape slipped again; reset the open right jaws to a simpler vertical grasp.
Retry a deeper, more central wrench-handle grasp, matching its latest orientation. Approach the tape now standing beside the box with a modest forward tilt.
Center the wrench deeper between the left jaws and close. Retreat the right wrist from its limit while increasing forward tilt toward the upright tape.
Let the deeper wrench grasp settle while lifting just clear of the table. Advance the tilted right jaws onto the upright tape body and close without changing orientation.
Lift the upright tape while keeping its full-body grasp unchanged. Reposition the left jaws over the wrench handle using the head view rather than the misleading overlapping wrist image.
Close and test the newly centered wrench grasp with a short lift. Approach the standing tape from its outer side for a controlled inward repositioning instead of another slipping lift.
Gently reposition the upright tape inward toward the box with the closed right jaws. Reopen and change the left jaw direction to avoid the front rim during the wrench grasp.
Reopen both jaws and lower to a more substantial body grasp, correcting the visible lateral and longitudinal offsets before closing again.
Correct both grasps backward toward the actual pad contact locations rather than the proximal wrist-image overlap, with only a shallow additional descent.
Close and briefly test the wrench at the corrected pad position. Clear the right arm completely from the box to reobserve the tape and restore a simple overhead approach.
Move the wrench slowly toward the left channel with only a small orientation change. Reapproach the now clearly visible tape from above with a modest forward tilt.
Approach the exposed wrench tip just outside the front rim with level jaws. Lower and tilt the right wrist so the pads reach the tape body rather than remaining above and behind it.
Clear the left arm from the toolbox. Lower the open right jaws progressively toward actual tape-contact depth while monitoring for obstruction, since the previous grasps remained too shallow.
Close on the tape at the newly established contact depth and make a short lift. Approach the clearly exposed wrench handle with a matching level grasp.
Shift the wrench laterally between the pads. Reopen and advance the tape grasp farther onto its body, with a small extra tilt and lower depth, then close both.
